personality_one_liner: A highly legible, data-dense, and professional finance aesthetic that grounds operations in trust and clarity through structure and typography.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room for forms. Follow iOS rhythms. Use md for inner component padding and lg/xl for outer container margins.

do's: Use frosted glass on the bottom tab bar
Use on sticky headers over scrolling content
dont's: Never apply to form fields, chips, or body content

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: A high-level financial overview showing monthly totals, category breakdowns, and paid vs. outstanding charts.

states.loading: Skeleton UI for metric cards and chart blocks.
states.empty: Illustration of the dairy farm logo with text 'No data logged for this month' and a button to 'Add Expense'.
states.error: Message 'Failed to load dashboard' with a Retry button.

screens.layout: Display current month's income and expenses as oversized metric cards at the top. Below, use a stacked bar chart for Paid vs Outstanding amounts. Under that, a list of top expense categories. All sections wrapped in 'surfaceSecondary' cards with 'md' radius and 'shadow_tier 1' on 'surface' background.

screens.name: Expenses List
screens.purpose: A filterable, paginated ledger of all recorded expenses.

states.empty: Crumpled receipt illustration stating 'No expenses found' with 'Add Expense' CTA.

screens.layout: Sticky header with horizontally scrolling filter chips (Category, Payment Status, Month). Below, a flat list of transaction rows. Each row: Icon (tinted by category), Vendor & Date (left), Amount & Status Badge (right). The list should have a floating action button (FAB) at the bottom right for 'New Expense' using glassmorphism.

screens.name: Add/Edit Expense
screens.purpose: A data-dense form to record all aspects of an expense, invoice, and payment.

states.error: Inline validation errors below inputs in 'error' color.

screens.layout: Single-column scrollable form grouped into iOS-native grouped sections. Group 1: Basics (Date, Vendor, Cost Centre). Group 2: Categorization (Main, Sub, Head). Group 3: Financials (Amount, GST%, GST Amt, TDS, Taxable, Total). Group 4: Payment (Status segmented control, Mode, Paid, Outstanding). Group 5: Remarks. Inputs use labels above fields. Submit CTA is sticky at the bottom over a glass or solid background, inside a KeyboardAvoidingView.

screens.name: Vendors & Categories
screens.purpose: Management interface to add, edit, and disable vendors and categories.
screens.layout: Segmented control at the top to toggle between Vendors and Categories. Simple list views beneath with swipe-to-edit or tap-to-open-sheet behavior. 'Add' button in the top right header.

dashboard_empty_farm.alt: Dairy milk bottle representing the Paavni brand

receipt_empty.alt: A crumpled official receipt representing no transactions found

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly adhere to the 'iOS-Native Clean' personality.
Do not use ANY blue, indigo, or purple. Stick to the brand palette of forest and sage green provided.
For the data-dense Add Expense form, use clear iOS grouped table view styles to chunk the form (Basics, Categorization, Financials, Payment, Remarks). This prevents cognitive overload.
The primary action (Save Expense) must be a sticky floating CTA at the bottom of the form, ensuring users don't have to scroll to the very bottom to submit.
Status badges (Paid, Outstanding, Unpaid, Partly Paid) should leverage the 'success', 'warning', and 'error' tokens.
Implement the gradient-to-dark scrim pattern for any text over the dashboard/empty state imagery.
